sections.title: Usage notes
sections.what: Explains how to run the importer: check the quotes first, dry run, then commit with the approved digest, then register the batch in the replay ledger.
sections.why: The header is the operating procedure for this importer.

sections.name: populationCli
sections.title: Run the import from the command line
sections.what: Reads the flags and file names, stops with a usage message if no file is given, runs the import for the chosen industry, prints a summary, and also runs this same logic when the file is started directly.
sections.why: Reason for the direct-run block not stated in the code. It most likely lets the file be run as a command.
sections.watch_out: If the direct-run check fails on a given system, the import silently never starts.

summary: A shared command-line tool that imports researched population batches for a named industry. It runs as a dry run unless committed with an approved digest.
purpose: Provide one importer that works for any industry registered in the population list.
why: The header describes it as the general importer for any registered manifest, replacing an industry-specific one.
how: The populationCli function reads the flags and reply file names, stops with a usage message if no file is given, runs the shared import for the industry, and prints the mode, counts, digests, and report path. The file also runs this function directly when started as a script.
inputs: The population key, one or more reply files, and the flags --commit, --approved-digest, and --report-name.
outputs: A JSON summary on the console, and whatever the shared import writes.
risks: The direct-run check compares a file address with the script path, which may not match on some systems, so the script could do nothing when started directly. A commit needs the exact approved digest.
debug: Run the quote check first, as the header says. Read the usage message if the command is refused. After a commit, confirm the batch is registered in the replay ledger, or it will not load on the main database.
